## Core Principles

### I. Preserve Existing Public API Behavior
All changes to TinyDB MUST maintain backward compatibility with the existing public API. No modification, removal, or behavioral change to any documented public method, class, or module interface is permitted without explicit justification and version bump. Rationale: Users depend on stable APIs; breaking changes must be avoided to preserve trust and reduce migration burden.

### II. Attach Testable Acceptance Criteria to Requirements
Every requirement MUST have explicit, testable acceptance criteria defined before implementation begins. Acceptance criteria must be verifiable through automated tests with clear pass/fail conditions. Rationale: Testable criteria eliminate ambiguity and provide objective evidence of requirement fulfillment.

### III. Distinguish Observed Evidence from Unverified Assertions
All claims about system behavior, performance, or correctness MUST be supported by observable evidence (test results, logs, metrics). Unverified assertions MUST be clearly labeled as such and tracked as open assumptions. Rationale: Evidence-based development prevents speculation from becoming embedded in the codebase.

### IV. Prefer Simple Scoped Implementations
Implementations MUST be scoped to the minimum necessary functionality to satisfy the requirement. Avoid over-engineering, premature abstraction, or features beyond the stated scope. Rationale: Simplicity reduces bugs, eases maintenance, and accelerates review cycles.

### V. Document Unresolved Assumptions and Regressions
All unresolved assumptions, known limitations, and identified regressions MUST be documented in the codebase (comments, docs, or tracking files). Undocumented gaps are considered violations. Rationale: Transparency about uncertainty enables informed decisions and prevents silent degradation.

## Code Quality Standards

All contributions MUST adhere to the following standards:
- Code must be readable and follow consistent style conventions
- Changes must include appropriate tests covering the modified behavior
- Documentation must be updated alongside code changes
- No new dependencies without justification and review

All development follows this workflow:
1. Requirements are specified with testable acceptance criteria
2. Tests are written before implementation (Red-Green-Refactor)
3. Implementation satisfies only the stated scope
4. All tests pass before merge
5. Unresolved assumptions are documented

## Governance

This constitution supersedes all other development practices within TinyDB. Amendments require:
- Documentation of the change and rationale
- Version increment per semantic versioning rules
- Explicit notation of any breaking principle changes

All PRs and reviews must verify compliance with these principles. Complexity must be justified with evidence. Use this constitution as the authoritative reference for development guidance.
